name: The Pearsons household
head: pearsons_hiram

arrival.note: 'Came in spring of 1833' - season precision, carried as the first day this project reads as spring.

party_size_on_arrival.note: Not attested in anything this project holds.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says where this household came from

reason_for_coming.value: The land sales and the canal expectation
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as speculator, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.trade_reasons.the_land_and_the_canal — the head's recorded trade is evidence about this household, and the draw it answered is the reason the record will carry until a source states one.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says why this household came, or a committed source that apportions the town's arrivals between the land sales, the canal and the harbour works

lives_at.note: Not attested in anything this project holds.

works_at.note: NOT MODELLED. No premises for this man is named in any source reached and none is in data/structures/.

present_on_scene_date.note: Treasurer of the city from 1837 and an alderman from its first election; continuous in the record on either side of the scene date.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

persons.name: Hiram Pearsons

associated_with.note: GROUND HE BOUGHT, WHICH IS NOT GROUND HE STOOD ON — the rung is `tract` for that reason, and `land_purchased` is in neither the home kinds nor the work kinds because a holding is not a place a man was. The federal tract-sale register carries 17 row(s) — ls0301, ls0302, ls0303, ls0304, ls0305, ls0306, ls0307, ls0308, ls0309, ls0310, ls0311, ls0312, ls0313, ls0314, ls0315, ls0316, ls0317 — to this purchaser, read as 'PEARSONS HIRAM', sorted onto school_section by tools/sort_land_sales_onto_tracts.py and covering about 69.12 acre(s) of it. THE TIER IS INFERRED AND THE TWO HALVES DIFFER: the purchase is documented — the register is a public record and states it — while the tie between that purchaser and THIS card is an identity ruling, upheld under T-0850 on 2026-09-10 by the rule 'PEARSONS HIRAM matches Hiram Pearsons: the forename names Hiram Pearsons of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full.'. The weaker half sets the tier. `to` is null because the register records a sale and not a tenure.

occupation.note: NO TRADE IS GIVEN. The roster says 'Hiram Pearson, came in spring of 1833'; Andreas's city rosters make him treasurer of Chicago in 1837, 1838 and 1839 and an alderman in 1837. 'Speculator' is this project's reading of a man who arrived in the spring before the land craze and ended as the city's treasurer, and it is a period-correct occupation that Andreas himself uses for others on the same page.

workplaces.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card pearsons_hiram (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.
